a11y.rule: Use role='alert' for critical messages that require immediate attention; use role='status' for less critical messages
a11y.quote: Use `role="alert"` for critical messages that require immediate attention.

relations.note: Use for a single form field error instead of Alert
relations.quote: you need to notify the user about an error in a single form field, use the component's own error message

relations.note: Use to summarise multiple errors instead of Alert
relations.quote: to summarise multiple errors

composition.rule: Avoid multiple alerts on the same page
composition.quote: Avoid multiple alerts on the same page, as it can confuse the user and make it difficult to understand what is important.

a11y.rule: Informative avatars must have an accessible name (e.g. via aria-label); if multiple avatars appear together, each name must be unique.
a11y.quote: Informative avatar must have an accessible name. The accessible name can be provided using aria-label . If multiple avatars are displayed together, each name must be unique.

a11y.rule: Decorative avatars must be hidden from screen readers when purely decorative and not conveying information.
a11y.quote: Decorative avatar must be hidden from screen readers. This applies when the avatar is purely decorative and does not convey information.

a11y.rule: A decorative avatar can be hidden when it appears alongside text that already identifies the person, e.g. inside a button.
a11y.quote: Example: If an avatar is shown inside a button with the text “Ola Nordmann”, the avatar can be hidden because the name already identifies the person.

a11y.rule: Clickable avatars must have an accessible name; avoid using just initials or the word "Avatar".
a11y.quote: Clickable avatar must have an accessible name. The accessible name can be provided using aria-label . Example: “Profile for Ola Nordmann”. Avoid: just initials or “Avatar”.

a11y.rule: The avatar must have an accessible name.
a11y.quote: Ensure the avatar has an accessible name .

a11y.rule: If you add an image or icon as content inside the avatar, set aria-hidden="true" to avoid duplicate information.
a11y.quote: If you add an image or icon as content inside the avatar, make sure to set aria-hidden="true" to avoid duplicate information.

a11y.rule: You must add an aria-label to the avatar yourself to explain who or what it represents.
a11y.quote: You must add an aria-label to the avatar yourself to explain who or what the avatar represents.

a11y.rule: Non-text children (like an image or icon) added inside Avatar automatically receive aria-hidden="true" to avoid duplicate information.
a11y.quote: If you add anything other than text as a child inside <Avatar> (like an image or icon), it will automatically receive aria-hidden="true" to avoid duplicate information.

relations.note: Use icons or other visual symbols instead of avatar when representing anything other than a person or an entity, such as a document.
relations.quote: Avoid avatar when representing anything other than a person or an entity, such as a document. Use icons or other visual symbols instead

composition.rule: Use avatar when representing a person or an entity.
composition.quote: Use avatar when representing a person or an entity

composition.rule: Avoid avatar when it is used purely for decoration without function or meaning.
composition.quote: it is used purely for decoration without function or meaning

composition.rule: Avatar can be round or square; use the chosen shape consistently throughout the solution.
composition.quote: Avatar can be round or square. Use them consistently throughout your solution.

composition.rule: Avatar should help make the user interface more recognisable and easier to navigate without distracting or taking up unnecessary space.
composition.quote: Avatar should help make the user interface more recognisable and easier to navigate without distracting or taking up unnecessary space.

composition.rule: Use the same avatar shape consistently throughout the solution.
composition.quote: Use the same avatar shape consistently throughout the solution.

composition.rule: Avatar should usually be combined with text, unless it is entirely clear who or what it represents.
composition.quote: The avatar should usually be combined with text, unless it is entirely clear who or what it represents.

composition.rule: Only use an avatar when it actually adds value to the user experience, e.g. to show who authored something or who is responsible.
composition.quote: Only use an avatar when it actually adds value to the user experience, for example to show who authored something or who is responsible.

composition.rule: Avatar should not contain text inside the component, except when using initials.
composition.quote: Avatar should not contain text inside the component, except when using initials.

composition.rule: Other text, such as full names, roles or organisations, should be placed outside the avatar to ensure good readability.
composition.quote: Other text, such as full names, roles or organisations, should be placed outside the avatar to ensure good readability.

composition.rule: The Avatar component should be able to be composed into other components.
composition.quote: The component should be able to be composed into other components.

a11y.rule: aria-label or aria-description can be used on the avatar stack to give screen readers context about what the stack represents
a11y.quote: aria-label or aria-description can be used on avatar stack to provide context to screen readers about what the stack represents.

a11y.rule: Avatars in an avatar stack can have tooltips and be links, but accessibility considerations must be kept in mind
a11y.quote: Avatars in avatar stack can have tooltips and be links, but be aware of accessibility considerations.

a11y.rule: tabindex="0" should be added to an expandable avatar stack (done automatically in React)
a11y.quote: tabindex="0" should be added, this is automatically added with expandable in React.

composition.rule: In plain HTML, build an avatar stack with the ds-avatar-stack class on a span, containing elements with the ds-avatar class
composition.quote: To create an avatar stack in plain HTML, use the ds-avatar-stack class on a <span> . Inside this, place elements with the ds-avatar class.

composition.rule: An avatar stack supports round and square avatar variants, but only one variant should be used per stack
composition.quote: Avatar stack supports both round and square variants, but only one variant per stack.

composition.rule: An avatar stack does not support wrapping across multiple lines
composition.quote: Avatar stack does not support wrapping across multiple lines.

composition.rule: When there are more avatars than fit in the stack, a suffix can be used to show the count as text to the right of the stack
composition.quote: If there are more avatars than can fit in the stack, you can use suffix to indicate this as text to the right of the stack.

a11y.rule: Badge used without text inside it must have accompanying text next to it
a11y.quote: Badge can be used without text inside it, but it must then have accompanying text next to it.

a11y.rule: Information should not be communicated through colour or shape alone
a11y.quote: Information should not be communicated through colour or shape alone.

a11y.rule: A badge showing important information must be included in the interactive element's accessible name
a11y.quote: Badge that shows important information must be included in the interactive element’s accessible name.

a11y.rule: A badge that changes value must be announced to screen readers
a11y.quote: Badge that changes value (for example 1 → 2) must be announced to screen readers

relations.note: Avoid Badge when interactive actions are required; use Chip instead
relations.quote: interactive actions are required, use chip or button instead

relations.note: Avoid Badge when interactive actions are required; use Button instead
relations.quote: interactive actions are required, use chip or button instead

relations.note: Badge is not intended for text; use Tag to display words or short phrases
relations.quote: This component is not intended for text. If you need to display words or short phrases, use Tag instead.

composition.rule: Badge can be placed next to other text or components
composition.quote: Badge can be placed next to other text or components.

composition.rule: To float a badge, the ds-badge--position class must be used on a wrapper around the element the badge is placed over
composition.quote: If you want it to be floating, the class ds-badge--position must be used on a wrapper around the element that the badge is to be placed over.

a11y.rule: Breadcrumbs must be handled so that the trail does not become too long on small screens; if it becomes too long, it should be replaced with a back link.
a11y.quote: Breadcrumbs must be handled so that it does not become too long on small screens. Check that the breadcrumb trail does not extend beyond the visible area at a narrow viewport or high zoom. If the trail becomes too long, it should be replaced with a back link.

a11y.rule: Skip link must bypass breadcrumbs and go directly to the main content, so users can skip repeated content without navigating through the breadcrumbs.
a11y.quote: Skip link must bypass breadcrumbs and go directly to the main content. Users should be able to skip repeated content without navigating through the breadcrumbs.

a11y.rule: Link text in breadcrumbs must be understandable; avoid generic names or unclear abbreviations.
a11y.quote: The link text in breadcrumbs must be understandable. Avoid generic names or unclear abbreviations.

a11y.rule: Breadcrumbs must be consistently placed and structured across pages, appearing in the same location and following the same order everywhere they are used.
a11y.quote: Breadcrumbs must be consistently placed and structured across pages. The breadcrumb trail should appear in the same location and follow the same order on all pages where it is used.

a11y.rule: Breadcrumbs must not be the only way to navigate; users should have multiple ways to navigate to content.
a11y.quote: Breadcrumbs must not be the only way to navigate. Users should have multiple ways to navigate to content.

a11y.rule: The last link should correspond to the current page and be coded as a link with aria-current="page" so screen readers get correct information without other users mistaking it for a clickable link.
a11y.quote: The last link should correspond to the current page. It looks like regular text, but is coded as a link with aria-current="page" . This way, screen readers get the correct information about which page the user is on, without other users mistakenly perceiving it as a clickable link.

composition.rule: Use breadcrumbs when users may want to navigate back to previous levels.
composition.quote: Use breadcrumbs when users may want to navigate back to previous levels

composition.rule: Use breadcrumbs when users need help understanding where they are in the structure.
composition.quote: users need help understanding where they are in the structure

composition.rule: Avoid breadcrumbs when the navigation is linear, for example across steps in a workflow or a form.
composition.quote: Avoid breadcrumbs when the navigation is linear, for example across steps in a workflow or a form

composition.rule: On mobile or with a long trail, show only a link to the nearest parent page
composition.quote: On mobile, or when the breadcrumb trail becomes long, you can show only a link to the nearest parent page.

composition.rule: Be consistent: use either the back-link variant or the full breadcrumb trail, not both
composition.quote: Be consistent in your approach, and use either this variant or the full breadcrumb trail, not both.

composition.rule: Breadcrumbs are only needed when there are three or more levels on a website.
composition.quote: Breadcrumbs are only needed when there are three or more levels on a website.

composition.rule: Breadcrumbs should always be placed at the top left of the page when using left-to-right text.
composition.quote: Breadcrumbs should always be placed at the top left of the page when using left-to-right text.

composition.rule: Breadcrumbs should appear below the menu and main navigation, but above the page title.
composition.quote: They should appear below the menu and main navigation, but above the page title.

composition.rule: For deep navigation, the component can be configured to show only the first and last parts of the trail on mobile, automatically on screens narrower than 650px.
composition.quote: For deep navigation, you can configure the component to show only the first and last parts of the trail on mobile. This can happen automatically on screens narrower than 650px, where only the link one level down is shown.

composition.rule: The text should match the page headings or navigation labels so that each level is easy to recognise.
composition.quote: The text should match the page headings or navigation labels so that each level is easy to recognise.

a11y.rule: An icon-only button needs an accessible label
a11y.quote: When the button has no text, you must add an accessible label describing what it does.

a11y.rule: An icon next to text must be hidden from screen readers
a11y.quote: When using an icon together with text, the icon should have `aria-hidden` so screen readers don't read unnecessary content.

relations.note: Use Link for navigation
relations.quote: navigating to other pages or out of the service, use Link instead

composition.rule: Only one primary button per page
composition.quote: There should be only one primary button per page.

a11y.rule: Link text in a card must clearly describe where the link goes; avoid generic text like 'Read more'
a11y.quote: Link text in card must clearly describe where the link goes. Use a clear title or link text that explains the destination. Avoid generic text such as “Read more” or “Click here”.

a11y.rule: The accessible name must match the visible text, even if overridden with aria-label or similar
a11y.quote: The accessible name must match the visible text. If you use aria-label or other techniques that override the accessible name, it must still match the visible text.

a11y.rule: Images in link cards must be decorative, with an empty alt attribute
a11y.quote: Images in link cards must be decorative. If the entire card is a link with an image, the image must not be informative and should have an empty alt attribute.

a11y.rule: Headings in a card must use the correct level relative to the rest of the page; do not skip heading levels
a11y.quote: Headings in card must use the correct level relative to the rest of the page. Do not skip heading levels (for example from h1 to h3 ).

a11y.rule: When Card renders as a button, its content loses all semantics, so this must be used carefully
a11y.quote: When the card is a button, the content inside loses all semantics, so use this carefully.

a11y.rule: Use <a> as the outermost element so screen readers read the whole card as one continuous link
a11y.quote: The entire card can be used as a link by using <a> as the outermost element. This is useful when you want all text and content in Card to be read by screen readers as one continuous link.

a11y.rule: Use data-clickdelegatefor to make a card with multiple interactive elements fully clickable while retaining the semantics of those elements
a11y.quote: If you have a card with multiple interactive elements, such as links or buttons, you can use data-clickdelegatefor to make the entire card clickable while retaining the semantics of the interactive elements.

a11y.rule: Prefer placing a link in the card's title over making the whole card a link, since screen reader users get a better experience
a11y.quote: If the card should link to another page, you can place a link in the card's title. The entire card then becomes clickable, but screen reader users get a better experience than if the whole card were a link (adrianroselli.com) .

a11y.rule: The keyboard focus ring should surround only the link text, not the entire card, so it matches the focus area for assistive technology users
a11y.quote: Note that with keyboard navigation, the focus ring only surrounds the text in the link, not the entire card. This is because link cards can also contain multiple clickable elements (secondary actions), and it is less confusing for users of assistive technology, such as voice control or screen readers, if the link text matches the focus area.

relations.note: Use Alert instead of Card for presenting important messages
relations.quote: important messages should be presented as alerts (use Alert instead)

composition.rule: Card can be divided into sections separated by dividers, which may include images or video extending to the edge
composition.quote: You can divide the card into sections. These get dividers between them and may include images or video that extend to the edge.

composition.rule: When using ds-card__block to create sections, all content must be placed inside block elements rather than directly in Card
composition.quote: If you need sections in the card, use ds-card__block if you want to divide the card with dividers or add images or video that extend to the edge. Note that when you use ds-card__block , all content must be placed inside elements with ds-card__block - not placed directly in Card .

composition.rule: Card blocks can be arranged horizontally by switching to flex or grid display
composition.quote: You can switch between display: flex and display: grid to place Card.Block next to each other:

composition.rule: data-clickdelegatefor is automatically added when Card finds a link inside its heading, for cards with text or media that navigate to another page
composition.quote: When Card finds an <a> inside the heading element, data-clickdelegatefor will automatically be added to the card. This is useful when Card contains text or media and should navigate to another page.

a11y.rule: Users must be able to move focus to Checkbox with Tab
a11y.quote: It must be possible to move focus to the Checkbox by pressing Tab on the keyboard.

a11y.rule: Users must be able to check and uncheck Checkbox with Space
a11y.quote: It must also be possible to check and uncheck it by pressing Space .

a11y.rule: A Checkbox must always have an accessible name
a11y.quote: A Checkbox must always have an accessible name.

a11y.rule: In special cases, aria-label or aria-labelledby may be used instead of a visible label
a11y.quote: In special cases, it may make sense to omit the <label> and instead use aria-label or aria-labelledby .

a11y.rule: Avoid using the disabled attribute where possible, for accessibility reasons
a11y.quote: Avoid using if possible for accessibility purposes

a11y.rule: Should avoid disabling checkbox because the disabled state can be hard to perceive and some users won't understand why an option isn't clickable
a11y.quote: We should avoid disabling ( disabled ) checkbox, because it can be difficult to perceive. Some users will not understand what the option means or why it is not clickable.

a11y.rule: Better to remove irrelevant checkbox options than to disable them
a11y.quote: If a checkbox or group of checkbox options is not relevant, it is usually better to remove them rather than disable them.

a11y.rule: If possible, explain to users why options are unavailable
a11y.quote: If possible, give users an explanation of why options are unavailable.

a11y.rule: Avoid using readOnly whenever possible because read-only fields can confuse users who don't understand why they can't change the content
a11y.quote: We avoid using readOnly whenever possible because such fields can be confusing. Not all users will understand why they cannot change the content.

a11y.rule: Read-only checkbox fields remain part of the tab order and their value is still included when the form is submitted
a11y.quote: Although they cannot be changed, fields with readOnly are still part of the tab order, and the information is included when the form is submitted.

a11y.rule: A read-only checkbox stops onClick and onChange but remains focusable
a11y.quote: If you set readonly on checkbox we ensure that it behaves as if it has read-only access by stopping onClick and onChange . The user will still be able to focus on the element.

a11y.rule: Horizontal checkbox lists can be challenging for users who need to enlarge text
a11y.quote: For users who need to enlarge the text, horizontal lists can be challenging.

relations.note: Use Radio instead of Checkbox when the user should choose only one option
relations.quote: the user should choose only one option; use a radio instead

relations.note: Use Select (or Suggestion) instead of Checkbox when the user must choose from more than seven options
relations.quote: the user must choose from more than seven options; use a select or suggestion instead

relations.note: Use Suggestion (or Select) instead of Checkbox when the user must choose from more than seven options
relations.quote: the user must choose from more than seven options; use a select or suggestion instead

relations.note: Use Switch instead of Checkbox when something should be turned on or off
relations.quote: something should be turned on or off; use a switch instead

composition.rule: A consent checkbox must always require an active action and must never be preselected, to ensure consent is voluntary
composition.quote: A checkbox for consent must always require an active action, and you should never preselect the box. This ensures that the consent is given voluntarily.

composition.rule: Checkbox is most often used in groups where the user can select more than one option
composition.quote: Most of the time, checkbox is used in groups where the user can select more than one option.

composition.rule: When checkboxes are grouped, the error message should be shown collectively for the whole group
composition.quote: When checkboxes are used in groups, the error message should be shown collectively for the entire group.

composition.rule: It may be appropriate to emphasise options with a larger click area (outline) around the checkbox in some cases
composition.quote: In some cases, it may be appropriate to emphasise options by using a larger click area around the checkbox.

composition.rule: Use fieldset for grouping multiple checkbox choices
composition.quote: Use fieldset for grouping multiple choices.

composition.rule: Checkbox is a composite component built from field, label, validation message, and input
composition.quote: Checkbox is a composite component that uses field , label , validation message , and input to create a checkbox.

composition.rule: Use useCheckboxGroup to create a parent checkbox that can select or clear all options in the group
composition.quote: Use useCheckboxGroup to create a parent checkbox that can select or clear all options in the group.

composition.rule: Sort answer options alphabetically unless there is a good reason to do otherwise
composition.quote: Sort the answer options alphabetically unless there is a good reason to do otherwise.

composition.rule: Response options should preferably be placed vertically for easier scanning and reading
composition.quote: Preferably place the response options vertically. This makes it easier to scan the list and read the options.

a11y.rule: Details is based on the native HTML <details> element, which provides good accessibility and semantics without extra JavaScript.
a11y.quote: The name comes from the built-in HTML <details> element, which provides good accessibility and semantics without additional JavaScript.

a11y.rule: Large amounts of text can be demanding for users, so details lets them decide what is relevant to read.
a11y.quote: Large amounts of text can be demanding for many users. Details allows users to decide for themselves what is relevant to read.

a11y.rule: Hidden content risks going unnoticed by users entirely.
a11y.quote: When content is hidden, there is a risk that users will not notice it at all.

a11y.rule: Nesting details makes it hard for users to understand what is open and closed.
a11y.quote: Nested lists can make it difficult for users to understand what is open and what is closed, especially when several levels can be expanded at once.

a11y.rule: Headings strongly affect whether users find, read, and can access the content.
a11y.quote: Headings can strongly influence whether users find what they need, whether the content is read, and whether it is considered accessible to all.

a11y.rule: Details is implemented as a native <details> element.
a11y.quote: Details is a native <details> element.

a11y.rule: A Firefox/Android Talkback bug is polyfilled so state and role are announced correctly.
a11y.quote: We polyfill a bug in Firefox when used with Android Talkback screen reader to announce state and role correctly.

a11y.rule: The component builds on the semantic HTML elements <details> and <summary>.
a11y.quote: For the Details component, we use u-details (github.io) , which builds on the semantic HTML elements <details> and <summary> .

a11y.rule: Space or Enter opens or closes the Details.
a11y.quote: Press Space or Enter to open or close the Details.

relations.note: Use error summary instead of details when you need to summarise error messages.
relations.quote: Avoid details when you need to show important content that everyone should see you need to display an action button you need to summarise error messages, use error summary instead

composition.rule: Use details for information relevant only to some users, for examples/FAQs, and where reading is optional.
composition.quote: Use details when you want to provide information that is only relevant to some users you want to give examples or answer frequently asked questions it should be up to the user whether they choose to read the content

composition.rule: Details can be placed inside a card to give the content a framed appearance.
composition.quote: You can use details inside a card to give the content a framed appearance.

composition.rule: Details inside a card gives the content a framed appearance; works well when it doesn't span the full page width or holds a single line
composition.quote: You can use details inside a card to give the content a framed appearance. This works well when details does not span the full width of the page, or when it contains only a single line.

composition.rule: Avoid using details just to make a page look tidier.
composition.quote: However, you should not use details to hide content just to make the page look tidier.

composition.rule: Do not nest one details inside another.
composition.quote: Do not place one details inside another.

composition.rule: The heading must clearly describe what the details contains.
composition.quote: Make sure the heading clearly describes what the details contains.

composition.rule: Vague headings like "Show more" or "Read more here" are not good enough.
composition.quote: “Show more” or “Read more here” are not good enough headings.

composition.rule: When there are many expandable sections, add a main or thematic heading above the whole list.
composition.quote: If you have many expandable sections, consider adding a main heading or thematic heading above the entire list.

composition.rule: Keep the content inside details short so it relates easily to the heading.
composition.quote: Keep the content inside details short so it is easy to relate to the heading.

composition.rule: If content is too long, split it into several details.
composition.quote: If the content is too long, divide it into several details.

composition.rule: For very large amounts of content, prefer separate pages over details.
composition.quote: For very large amounts of content, it may be better to create separate pages.

a11y.rule: Make sure elements receiving focus are not hidden behind the dialog
a11y.quote: Note: Make sure that elements receiving focus are not hidden behind the dialog .

a11y.rule: Add aria-haspopup="dialog" to the element that opens the dialog so screen reader users know it will open a dialog
a11y.quote: The attribute aria-haspopup="dialog" should be added to the element that opens the dialog to make it clear to screen reader users that it will open a dialog.

a11y.rule: Always provide a visible and simple way to close a dialog
a11y.quote: Always ensure that users have a visible and simple way to close a dialog.

a11y.rule: The close button (X) should stay visible even when the dialog's content requires scrolling
a11y.quote: The most common approach is a close button (X) in the top right corner. It should remain visible even when the dialog contains a lot of content and the user needs to scroll.

a11y.rule: In non-modal dialogs, elements receiving keyboard focus must not end up hidden behind the dialog
a11y.quote: When using non-modal dialogs, you must ensure that elements receiving focus through keyboard navigation do not end up behind the dialog and become hidden. See criteria 2.4.11 (w3.org) (AA) and 2.4.12 (w3.org) (AAA).

a11y.rule: Focusable elements must never be completely covered by the dialog during Tab navigation
a11y.quote: Ensure that focusable elements are never completely covered by the dialog when users navigate the page using the Tab key.

a11y.rule: Focus order must be logical and focus must always be visible
a11y.quote: Ensure that the focus order is logical and that focus is always visible, so users navigating with a keyboard or screen reader can understand where focus is located.

a11y.rule: Esc closes the dialog and returns focus to the trigger
a11y.quote: Esc closes the dialog (focus returns to the trigger)

relations.note: Use alert instead of a modal dialog when notifying users of something that does not require action
relations.quote: you need to notify users about something that does not require action. Use alert or a non-modal dialog instead

relations.note: Use popover instead of a modal dialog for short, optional information
relations.quote: you want to provide short, optional information, use popover

relations.note: Consult the system notifications pattern for guidance on when a modal dialog should be used
relations.quote: See also the system notifications pattern for more guidance on when a modal dialog should be used.

composition.rule: Using the placement prop, a dialog can behave like a drawer positioned from a given side
composition.quote: Using placement , dialog can behave like a so-called “drawer” from the position you specify.

composition.rule: Use multiple ds-dialog__block elements to divide the dialog with dividers into separate areas
composition.quote: Use multiple ds-dialog__block if you want to divide the dialog with dividers into, for example, a top and bottom area.

composition.rule: Content cannot be placed directly in the dialog if ds-dialog__block is used; all content must then be inside a block
composition.quote: Note that content cannot be placed directly in dialog if you use ds-dialog__block ; then all content should be inside one of the dialog's ds-dialog__block sections.

composition.rule: A close button that is the dialog's first direct child floats to the top right
composition.quote: If the button is a direct child of the dialog and the first element, it will float to the top right.

composition.rule: Use Dialog.TriggerContext together with Dialog.Trigger so the dialog and trigger can communicate without id/commandfor
composition.quote: Use Dialog.TriggerContext and Dialog.Trigger together, so Dialog can communicate without having to use id and commandfor .

composition.rule: Use buttons in the dialog to give users a clear path forward
composition.quote: Use buttons to give users a clear path forward.

a11y.rule: Apply aria-hidden="true" to the divider to avoid noise for screen reader users.
a11y.quote: Apply aria-hidden="true" to avoid noise in screen readers.

a11y.rule: Divider is a purely visual element and is not announced by screen readers.
a11y.quote: Divider is a purely visual element, and it is not announced by screen readers.

a11y.rule: Avoid using a divider solely for visual effect without functional meaning.
a11y.quote: However, avoid using a divider solely for visual effect without functional meaning.

a11y.rule: Since a divider represents a thematic separation, you must also use elements a screen reader can interpret to communicate that separation accessibly.
a11y.quote: A divider represents a thematic separation of content. To communicate this separation in an accessible way, you must also use elements that a screen reader can interpret.

composition.rule: Use divider when you want a clear separation between sections of content and whitespace alone does not provide sufficient separation.
composition.quote: Use divider when you want to create a clear separation between sections of content whitespace alone does not provide sufficient separation

composition.rule: Avoid divider when natural spacing or other visual elements already provide enough separation, since too many dividers create visual clutter.
composition.quote: Avoid divider when natural spacing or other visual elements provide enough separation too many divider elements create a cluttered visual appearance

composition.rule: Divider is used to break content into smaller sections for readability, and can also separate related content that still benefits from visual distinction.
composition.quote: Divider is used to break content into smaller sections, making it easier to read and understand. It can also be used to separate content that is related but still benefits from a visual distinction.

composition.rule: Use divider to mark a boundary between content that is not logically connected, such as different sections in an article or different functional areas on a page.
composition.quote: Use the component to mark a boundary between content that is not logically connected, such as different sections in an article or different functional areas on a page.

composition.rule: Use divider to visually clarify structure, not simply to fill empty space or decorate the page.
composition.quote: Use it to visually clarify the structure, not simply to fill empty space or “decorate” the page.

composition.rule: The accessible structural elements to pair with a divider can include a heading, a list, <section> elements, or elements with role="group".
composition.quote: This can include a heading , a list , <section> elements , or elements with role="group" .

a11y.rule: Dropdown does not create a semantic menu itself; it provides the foundation for building one yourself
a11y.quote: Dropdown does not create a semantic menu, but provides the foundation for building one yourself.

a11y.rule: The Popover API gives built-in accessibility for open/closed state and keyboard navigation.

composition.quote: If the page includes a cookie banner or similar message, place the skip link immediately after that element in the code.

composition.rule: Add the class ds-skip-link to an <a> tag pointing to the main content, and the target should be focusable via tabindex="-1"
composition.quote: Add the class name ds-skip-link to an <a> tag that points to the main content of the page. The target should be able to receive focus with tabindex="-1" .

a11y.rule: The spinner should be combined with text or have an aria-label so assistive technology users know loading is in progress
a11y.quote: To ensure a good user experience, the spinner should be combined with text or have an aria-label , so that users of assistive technologies are informed that loading is in progress.

a11y.rule: When loading text is shown together with a spinner, the spinner must be hidden with aria-hidden="true" to prevent duplicate announcements
a11y.quote: When you display text indicating loading together with a spinner, you must hide the spinner using aria-hidden="true" to prevent “loading” from being announced multiple times.

a11y.rule: If no text is included, the spinner should instead have an aria-label
a11y.quote: If you do not include text, the spinner should instead have an aria-label .

relations.note: Avoid spinner when only specific parts of the page are loading; use skeleton instead
relations.quote: Avoid spinner when only specific parts of the page are loading — consider using skeleton instead

composition.rule: Spinner can be used inside a button, a field, or another defined area where the user is waiting for something like saving or updating content
composition.quote: It can be used in a button, a field, or another defined area where the user is waiting for something to happen, such as saving or updating content.

composition.rule: Explanatory text can be shown alongside the spinner to describe why the user has to wait
composition.quote: In some cases, it may improve the user experience to show explanatory text alongside the spinner, describing why the user has to wait.

relations.note: Use Radio or Checkbox when there are only a few options
relations.quote: users need to choose between only a few options

composition.rule: Keep each option short
composition.quote: Each option should be short

a11y.rule: Use role="switch" so screen readers identify the toggle switch and its on/off state.
a11y.quote: We use role="switch" to inform screen readers that this is a toggle switch.

a11y.rule: This role tells screen reader users that the control is a switch that can be turned on and off.
a11y.quote: This allows screen readers to tell the user that it is a switch and that it can be turned on and off.

a11y.rule: Do not add aria-checked, since it is unnecessary on a switch built as a checkbox input.
a11y.quote: We do not add aria-checked because it is not necessary when the switch is an input with type="checkbox" .

a11y.rule: Space toggles the switch on and off via keyboard.
a11y.quote: Space toggles the switch on and off

a11y.rule: Label text should make sense when read aloud with an on/off switch announced at the end (for screen reader users).
a11y.quote: The text should make sense when you read it aloud and add an on/off switch at the end.

relations.note: When users are answering questions in a form, use radio instead of switch.
relations.quote: users are answering questions in forms, use radio or checkbox instead

relations.note: When users are answering questions in a form, use checkbox instead of switch.
relations.quote: users are answering questions in forms, use radio or checkbox instead

relations.note: When users are switching between different content views (e.g. list vs graph), use toggleGroup instead of switch.
relations.quote: users are switching between different content views, such as list and graph, use toggleGroup instead

relations.note: When content needs to be filtered, use chip instead of switch.
relations.quote: content needs to be filtered, use chip instead

composition.rule: Use fieldset to group multiple switch components together.
composition.quote: Use fieldset to group multiple switch components together.

composition.rule: By default, the switch is placed on the left and its label on the right.
composition.quote: As a rule, the switch is placed on the left and the label on the right.

composition.rule: When switches are fixed on the right side of the interface, place the label on the left so switches align neatly on the right.
composition.quote: In some cases, switches are fixed on the right side of the interface. In those situations, it is best to place the label on the left, so all switches align neatly on the right.

composition.rule: Build the switch using the ds-input classname on an input with type="checkbox" and role="switch".
composition.quote: Use the classname ds-input on <input> along with type="checkbox" and role="switch" .

composition.rule: For a valid form element, use ds-field together with a label.
composition.quote: For a valid form element, we recommend using <ds-field> together with a <label> .

a11y.rule: Table cells must not be merged, and each cell should contain only one interactive element
a11y.quote: Table cells should not be merged, and each cell should contain only one interactive element.

a11y.rule: Use row and/or column headers so screen reader users can navigate the table
a11y.quote: For screen reader users to navigate the content, it is important to use row and/or column headers ( <Table.HeaderCell> ).

a11y.rule: Mark headers with scope="row" or scope="col" to indicate what they apply to
a11y.quote: Use scope="row" and scope="col" to indicate whether the header applies to a row or a column.

a11y.rule: Headers may be visually hidden if space is limited
a11y.quote: If space is limited, you may visually hide one or more headers.

a11y.rule: Tables must always include a caption describing what the table shows, since screen readers read it first
a11y.quote: Tables must always include a caption element that provides a brief description of what the table shows. Screen readers will read the caption, allowing users to decide whether they want to continue reading the table.

a11y.rule: Empty cells must use Table.Cell so screen readers can navigate the table correctly
a11y.quote: Empty cells must use Table.Cell . This is important to ensure that screen readers can navigate the table correctly.

a11y.rule: Make sure sorting can be changed using the keyboard
a11y.quote: Make sure you can change the sorting using the keyboard.

a11y.rule: Test sorting with a screen reader to confirm sortable state, sort direction, and that focus isn't lost when sorting changes
a11y.quote: Test with a screen reader to verify that you hear what is sortable, the sorting types, and that focus is not lost when sorting changes.

a11y.rule: Tables are challenging on mobile; common adaptations are horizontal scroll or converting to a list view
a11y.quote: Tables can be challenging on mobile, as there is no universal design that works well in all contexts. The most common approaches are a table that scrolls horizontally or converting the table into a list view.

relations.note: Prefer a list view over a table when the content is better suited to a list
relations.quote: the information is better suited to a list or card view

relations.note: Prefer a card view over a table when the content is better suited to cards
relations.quote: the information is better suited to a list or card view

composition.rule: Use table to compare information, present clearly structured row/column data, or support sorting
composition.quote: Use table when the goal is to help users compare information easily the data needs a clear structure with rows and columns the content can benefit from sorting

composition.rule: Avoid table for page layout, when content is very limited without need for comparison, or when large data sets become hard to read on mobile
composition.quote: Avoid using table when the purpose is to create layout or visually organise content on a page the information is better suited to a list or card view the content is very limited, for example only one column or very few data points without a need for comparison the table becomes difficult to read on mobile because the data set is large

composition.rule: Use table to structure and present data clearly in rows and columns
composition.quote: Use table to structure and present data clearly in rows and columns.

composition.rule: Content should be left-aligned except numbers, which should be right-aligned for easier comparison
composition.quote: Content in tables should be left-aligned, except for numbers, which should be right-aligned to make comparison easier.

composition.rule: Use Table.HeaderCell (not Table.Cell) for cells that describe the content of their row or column
composition.quote: Use <Table.HeaderCell> for header cells, not <Table.Cell> . A cell counts as a header when it describes the content of the same row or column.

composition.rule: In rows with several actions, a menu can be used to save space when the actions don't need to be visible at all times
composition.quote: In table rows with several actions, you can use a menu to save space if the actions do not need to be visible at all times.

composition.rule: When numbers are meant to be compared, align them to the right within the cell
composition.quote: When numbers appear in a table and are meant to be compared, align them to the right within the cell.

composition.rule: Avoid long texts in table cells; keep content short and concise so it's easy to scan across rows and columns
composition.quote: Avoid long texts in table cells. Keep content short and concise so it is easy to scan across rows and columns.

composition.rule: If more information is needed than fits in a cell, consider linking to a detail page
composition.quote: If you need to show more information, consider linking to a detail page.

composition.rule: Use headers to tell users what type of content they'll find in rows and columns
composition.quote: Use headers to tell users what type of content they will find in the rows and columns.

composition.rule: Content in cells should generally be left-aligned; exceptions are numbers, currency, and sometimes form elements and buttons
composition.quote: As a general rule, content in cells should be left-aligned to make it easier to read and scan. The exception is numbers and currency and sometimes form elements and buttons.

a11y.rule: Icons used in tabs must be intuitive and have descriptive titles for screen readers.
a11y.quote: Ensure that the icons are intuitive and have descriptive titles for screen readers.

a11y.rule: When icons are combined with text, the icons should be decorative and marked with aria-hidden.
a11y.quote: Icons should be decorative and marked with aria-hidden .

a11y.rule: Use the ds-tabs component rather than building a custom tabs implementation, to ensure good accessibility and functionality.
a11y.quote: We recommend using <ds-tabs> , and not building your own tabs from scratch, to ensure good accessibility and functionality.

a11y.rule: Each tab must have a unique title.
a11y.quote: Each tab must have a unique title

a11y.rule: Icons used in tabs must be decorative (aria-hidden) or have descriptive titles.
a11y.quote: When using icons, ensure they are decorative ( aria-hidden ) or have descriptive titles

a11y.rule: If a tab panel has no focusable elements, the panel itself receives focus.
a11y.quote: If a tab panel does not contain any focusable elements, the panel itself receives focus

a11y.rule: Tabs support keyboard navigation with arrow keys.
a11y.quote: Tabs supports keyboard navigation with arrow keys

composition.rule: Use tabs when content needs structuring without loading a new page, when information benefits from being divided into clearly labelled sections, and when navigation becomes easier without viewing all content at once.
composition.quote: Use tabs when content needs to be structured without loading a new page information benefits from being divided into clearly labelled sections navigation becomes easier when users do not need to view all content at once

composition.rule: Avoid tabs when an immediate overview is needed, when information must be compared across sections, for step-by-step processes where order matters, for large amounts of content, or when the content could be shown on a single page or spread across several pages.
composition.quote: Avoid using tabs when it is important to give an immediate overview of the content information needs to be compared across sections users must go through a step-by-step process where the order matters large amounts of content may slow down the page the content could just as well be shown on a single page or spread across several pages

composition.rule: Before choosing tabs, consider simplifying content, distributing it across pages, keeping it on a single page with clear headings, or using a table of contents.
composition.quote: Before choosing tabs, consider whether it might be better to: simplify and reduce the amount of content distribute the content across several pages keep everything on a single page with clear headings use a table of contents for easier navigation

composition.rule: Limit the number of tabs, since too many make it hard to get an overview, especially on small screens.
composition.quote: Limit the number of tabs - too many make it difficult to get an overview, especially on small screens

composition.rule: Use clear, descriptive tab names since tabs hide content and it must be obvious what each section contains.
composition.quote: Use clear, descriptive names - tabs hide content, so it must be obvious what each section contains

composition.rule: Place the most important content first, organising tabs according to users' needs.
composition.quote: Place the most important content first - organise tabs according to users' needs

composition.rule: Keep tabs on a single line, since long labels or too many tabs make navigation harder.
composition.quote: Keep tabs on a single line - long labels or too many tabs make navigation harder

composition.rule: Avoid disabled tabs; remove them or explain why they contain no content.
composition.quote: Avoid disabled tabs - remove them or explain why they contain no content

composition.rule: Tab labels should be short and descriptive so users understand what they will find when clicking.
composition.quote: Tabs labels should be short and descriptive so users can easily understand what they will find when clicking.

composition.rule: Difficulty creating clear tab labels may indicate the content is not well structured.
composition.quote: If it is difficult to create clear labels, it may indicate that the content is not well structured.

composition.rule: If additional context is needed, a shared heading can be placed above the tabs component.
composition.quote: If additional context is needed, a shared heading can be placed above the tabs component.

a11y.rule: Group multiple Tags in a list so assistive tech announces them as a list, not one sentence
a11y.quote: If you are displaying several Tag components together, we recommend using a <ul> list with one <li> per Tag . This ensures that they are announced as a list rather than as one continuous sentence, providing a better experience for users of assistive technologies.

a11y.rule: Place multiple tags in a <ul>/<li> structure so screen readers announce them as a list
a11y.quote: When using multiple tags together, place them in a <ul> with <li> elements so screen readers announce them as a list.

relations.note: Use Link instead of Tag when linking to another page
relations.quote: linking to another page, use link instead

relations.note: Use Button instead of Tag when the element triggers an action
relations.quote: the element triggers an action, use button instead

relations.note: Use Chip instead of Tag when the user needs to filter content
relations.quote: the user needs to filter content, use chip instead

composition.rule: Tag should generally be placed after the title or name of the related element
composition.quote: Tag should generally be placed after the title or name of the related element.

composition.rule: Avoid placing tags next to buttons, as this can confuse users
composition.quote: Avoid placing tags next to buttons, as this can confuse users.

composition.rule: Icons can be used inside a tag to add additional visual information
composition.quote: Icons can be used inside a tag to add additional visual information.

composition.rule: Keep the padding on tag equal to the icon's margin when combining icon and text
composition.quote: We recommend keeping the padding on tag equal to the icon’s margin .

a11y.rule: Avoid disabling a textarea if possible, since it can be difficult for users to understand why the field cannot be used.
a11y.quote: Avoid disabling a textarea if possible. It can be difficult for users to understand why the field cannot be used.

a11y.rule: readOnly can be confusing since a text field is normally expected to be editable; use it only when truly necessary.
a11y.quote: Since a text field is normally expected to be editable, readOnly can be confusing. Use it only when it is truly necessary. In many cases, it is better to display the information as plain text rather than in a readOnly field.

a11y.rule: If readOnly is used, you must explain to the user why the content cannot be edited.
a11y.quote: Important: If you choose to use readOnly , you must explain to the user why the content cannot be edited.

a11y.rule: Fields with the readonly attribute remain part of the tab order.
a11y.quote: Fields with the readonly attribute remain part of the tab order.

relations.note: Use textfield instead of textarea when short answers are expected.
relations.quote: Avoid using textarea when short answers are expected, use textfield instead

relations.note: For structured/fixed-choice answers, break the question into smaller parts and use components like Radio instead of a free-text textarea.
relations.quote: Be aware that some users find free-text fields challenging. In certain cases, it may be better to break the question into smaller, more structured parts and let users answer with components such as Radio .

relations.note: Textarea should also follow the general guidelines defined for textfield.
relations.quote: In addition to these recommendations, follow the general guidelines for textfield

composition.rule: The height of the textarea should reflect the expected amount of text.
composition.quote: The height of the textarea should reflect the expected amount of text.

composition.rule: Textarea should expand in height when users need more space.
composition.quote: Textarea should expand in height when users need more space.

composition.rule: A textarea should not be wider than 50-75 characters including spaces.
composition.quote: A textarea should not be wider than 50-75 characters including spaces.

a11y.rule: A textfield must always have a label
a11y.quote: A textfield must always have a label.

a11y.rule: Prefixes and suffixes must not be used without a label
a11y.quote: These must **not** be used without a `<label>`, since screen readers will not announce them.

a11y.rule: Information in a prefix or suffix must also appear in the label
a11y.quote: The information shown in the prefix or suffix must also be reflected in the label text.

a11y.rule: Autocomplete is required where a predefined purpose exists
a11y.quote: Autocomplete is required in fields where a predefined purpose exists, as defined in 1.3.5

relations.note: Use Input for a simple field without form logic
relations.quote: you need a simple input field without form logic, use input instead

composition.rule: Textfield bundles label, help text and validation message
composition.quote: you need a complete form field with label, help text, and validation message

a11y.rule: Icon-only toggles need a tooltip to convey meaning
a11y.quote: Use tooltip to clarify the actions when using icons alone.

relations.note: Use Radio when the options are answers in a form
relations.quote: the options represent answers in a form

relations.note: Use Switch for an on/off setting
relations.quote: the choice is an on/off setting

composition.rule: At least two options, few enough to fit on one line
composition.quote: A toggle group should have at least two options, but not so many that they no longer fit horizontally.

composition.rule: The group needs a label explaining what the options refer to
composition.quote: Include a label for the group that explains what the options refer to.

a11y.rule: Tooltip must not be used as a substitute for alt text or title attributes
a11y.quote: Tooltip should never be used as a replacement for alt text or title .

a11y.rule: Tooltip is less suitable on touch devices since it normally relies on hover or focus, which touch does not support
a11y.quote: On touch devices, Tooltip is less suitable because it is normally triggered by hover or focus , which are not supported on these devices.

relations.note: Use popover instead of tooltip when the explanation is longer than four words
relations.quote: the explanation is longer than four words, use popover instead

relations.note: Use popover instead of tooltip when the content contains links or other interactive elements
relations.quote: the content contains links or other interactive elements, use popover instead

relations.note: Use popover instead of tooltip when richer content such as longer text, images, or buttons is needed
relations.quote: If richer content is needed - for example longer text, images, or buttons - use a popover instead.

relations.note: The Tooltip `open` prop is deprecated for overriding open state; use Popover instead
relations.quote: This should not be used on Tooltip. Use a Popover instead

composition.rule: Tooltip provides brief supplementary information without distracting from the main content
composition.quote: Tooltip provides brief supplementary information without distracting from the main content.

composition.rule: Tooltip is not intended for information essential to completing a task
composition.quote: Tooltip is not intended for information that is essential for completing a task.

composition.rule: Important content should appear as body text or help text on the page, not in a tooltip
composition.quote: Important content should instead appear as body text or help text on the page.

composition.rule: Use tooltip when a symbol needs explanation, an interactive element's action needs clarifying, or keyboard shortcuts need to be shown
composition.quote: Use tooltip when a symbol needs a brief explanation the action of an interactive element needs to be clarified keyboard shortcuts need to be shown

composition.rule: Avoid using tooltip when the text is already visible on the page
composition.quote: Avoid using tooltip when the text is already visible on the page

composition.rule: Consider whether the tooltip should be placed above, below, or beside the element
composition.quote: Consider whether the tooltip should be placed above, below, or beside the element.

composition.rule: A tooltip should not contain more than one sentence or more than four words, to avoid obstructing other important elements on screen
composition.quote: A tooltip should not contain more than one sentence or more than four words, to avoid obstructing other important elements on the screen.

composition.rule: Tooltip should not repeat text that is already present on the page
composition.quote: Tooltip should not repeat text that is already present on the page.

composition.rule: Tooltip content should provide additional help or clarification that is not immediately obvious
composition.quote: It should provide additional help or clarification that is not immediately obvious.

a11y.rule: Messages should be placed close to the field they relate to
a11y.quote: Messages should be placed close to the field they relate to, so that both visual users and users of assistive technologies can easily understand the connection.
